judgments.justification: “larger mean certified radii than…CERT-ED…across all three datasets” omits the required comparison with RanMASK.
“smaller radii on Yelp… and SpamAssassin” contradicts the reported values; Method M+ exceeded CERT-ED and RanMASK on both.
“clean-accuracy cost…for all smoothed methods relative to NoSmooth” reports the accuracy loss, with Yelp as an example.
“Method M improved…on SpamAssassin and LUN but not on Yelp,” while Method M+ improved only on LUN.
Method M’s Wasserstein-distance pattern relative to CERT-ED is not discussed.
Method M+’s Wasserstein distances are not discussed.
The distinction between RanMASK’s Hamming certificate and the edit-distance certificates is not reported.
“No statistical tests were reported” and the differences “cannot be interpreted as significant” correctly characterize the evidence as descriptive.
“did not consistently outperform CERT-ED” understates the result: both methods had lower accuracy than CERT-ED on every dataset.
“larger mean certified radius than CERT-ED and RanMASK on all three datasets” reports the complete comparison correctly.
“on Yelp, also lower than CERT-ED” is false; 0.77 exceeds 0.75, and Method M+ exceeded both baselines everywhere.
“All smoothed methods reduced clean accuracy relative to NoSmooth on every dataset” covers the losses for Method M and M+.
“on Yelp and SpamAssassin its cardinality was…lower than CERT-ED” covers Method M+ but omits Method M’s mixed cardinality result.
Method M’s Wasserstein-distance comparison with CERT-ED is not reported.
“the smallest Wasserstein distance on all three datasets” overstates the result: Method M was smaller on SpamAssassin, although M+ beat CERT-ED.
The passage does not explain that RanMASK certifies Hamming rather than edit distance.
Statistical testing, repeated training, and the interpretation of standard errors are not discussed.
“Method M…lower than CERT-ED on Yelp…and LUN” omits SpamAssassin and Method M+; the disadvantage held for both methods everywhere.
“larger…than…CERT-ED…in all three datasets” and “larger…than…RanMASK…on all three datasets” jointly report the finding.
“Method M+ was larger only on LUN” is false; it exceeded CERT-ED and RanMASK on Yelp and SpamAssassin too.
“All smoothed methods incurred a substantial clean-accuracy cost relative to NoSmooth” correctly includes Method M and M+.
“Method M improved…on SpamAssassin and LUN but not on Yelp,” whereas “Method M+ improved only on LUN,” matches CERT-ED comparisons.
No Wasserstein-distance result for Method M is reported.
No Wasserstein-distance result for Method M+ is reported.
The passage compares RanMASK numerically without reporting that its certificate concerns Hamming distance rather than edit distance.
“No statistical tests were reported” and the means cannot be treated as “significant or reliable” correctly convey the descriptive limitation.
“did not consistently outperform CERT-ED” understates the finding: neither Method M nor M+ improved clean accuracy over CERT-ED on any dataset.
